summary: COMPUTE SAIL (baseline): a 279 m square film flown as a diamond (395 m corner to corner), 69543 m2, tensioned at its 4 corners by 4 diagonal 199 m triangular-truss Mg booms behind the film (constant-force tensioners, N = 0.1 N/m, 4 % catenary edges). Non-spinning: spin was rejected because the precession torque that 0.5 % corner vanes can supply limits the spin period to >= ~45 min, giving 0.6-10 mN/m of tension and a 1-3 m edge-bending length, so the 1.63 m fold panels would curl. 1.06e+08 chiplet sites (one 1e8-chip training replica + spares) at 25.4 mm pitch, 14.8 MW to the cores, 14.4 t (0.207 kg/m2, 0.98 g/W; 1.07 g/W with the 10 % overbuild used in research3). The film stack is the architecture stack with the back enamel thickened from 5 to 15 um: the thin-film IR model gives eps_b ~0.61 for 5 um. Front face: no metal (IBC cells), AR-coated glass over textured c-Si, near-black navy (luminous albedo ~0.002-0.005), a magenta-blue AR glint 0.13 % of the Sun. Dark 25 mm hinge strips every 1.63 m. Chiplets, 60 patch laser terminals, hub and booms are all on the back; four 87 m2 Al corner vanes are the brightest parts. POD (parametric, 1 MW): dense memory+logic stack (1.5 m3/MW, 0.8 t/MW) in a 5 g/cm2 Mg/MgO shield, 4431 m2 of wings, 973 m2 of edge-on radiators (4 blades), 4 SO2 two-phase loops, about 4 g/W, 172 x 204 m. Pods that serve sails must fly in the film shell: Starlink-class links close only within ~3,000 km, and 0.86-0.90 AU is >= 3e6 km away. Training islands: 12+1 pods on a 1 km projected circular orbit, shadow-free.

baseline_dims.shape: square flown as a diamond, catenary (scalloped) edges
baseline_dims.range_note: 87 m holds a 1e7-chip replica (or 1e8 sites at 10x memory/site); 500 m if power/site rises to 0.5 W at the same replica

sizing_rationale.replica: the largest film training replica (1e8 chiplets) must be one contiguous mesh: 1.03e8 sites incl. 3 % spares -> 279 m side
sizing_rationale.fixed_mass: hub + vanes + tensioners ~0.34 t = 2.4 % of the sail; at a 1e7-chip sail (82 m) fixed mass would be ~19 %
sizing_rationale.fault_domain: 14.8 MW per sail; booms SF 3 with 2 tethers per corner; a cut tether or edge cable slackens one edge, power loss is small (cos)
sizing_rationale.launch_package: 14.4 t, 2 film rolls R 1.09 m x 1.63 m + 3.4 m hub; fits one mass-driver package (100 g) with a separate EP kick stage

structure.architecture: frame + 4 diagonal booms (non-spinning); constant-force corner tensioners; 4 % catenary edges; film attached at the 4 corners only (loose central tether)

booms.type: triangular truss, 3 thin-wall Mg-alloy (AZ-type) tube longerons, Mg-alloy battens + Fe-Ni wire diagonals
booms.position: root at hub; along +X,-X,+Y,-Y; flat face (2 longerons) 0.30 m behind the film, apex longeron at z = -0.30 - 0.866*side

flatness.driver: CTE mismatch of the 13 um Mg spreader (free curvature 0.122 /m/K), acting only at free edges (hinge strips, rim) over ell = sqrt(D/N)
flatness.power_cost: edge zones (~22 % of area) tilted <= 3.7 deg: cos loss < 0.2 %
flatness.requirement: laminate stress-free at 348 K (process at 340-355 K), residual moment <= 3 K-equivalent; fallback stack C (c-Si 46 um as spreader, kappa 3.3x lower, +0.02 kg/m2)

spin.reason: precession torque H*n_orbit vs 0.5 % vanes caps spin at a period of >= ~45 min (x2 margin); tension then 0.6-10 mN/m, ell = 2.3 m > 0.81 m half-panel -> fold panels curl (48 deg at 3 K); billow 1.8 deg

rejected.hoop_ring: in-plane buckling ring mass is comparable, but a 1.2 km-circumference compression hoop has no packaging/deployment path from a 3 m package
rejected.hex_tiles_cable_net: needs a compression member or spin anyway; a hex outline breaks the square chiplet mesh alignment (gores at 60 deg)
rejected.frame_rigid: rigidly attached film would see dN = 3178 N/m from a 3e-4 film/boom strain mismatch: tensioners must be load-defined springs

meteoroids.note: Holes do not grow: at spin tension the laminate stress is ~71 Pa, and the Griffith crack length is 3.6e+07 m. Rip-stops are needed only for handling/deployment loads; the 25 mm hinge strips (glass-cloth) every 1.63 m and the diagonal tapes act as rip-stops. A hit kills at most its 25 mm tile (0.15 W).

structure.rip_stop: not needed for tear arrest: at 1.2 kPa membrane stress the Griffith crack length is ~1e+05 m. Hinge strips (every 1.63 m) and the hem bound damage during handling/deployment; expected holes >= 3 mm: 3.5 per sail per year; >= 10 mm: one per ~33 years

segmentation.cell: 2 half-cells 25.4 x 12.7 mm in series per tile (IBC, rear contacts)

hinge_strips.material: dark-enamelled glass cloth with Al jumpers

stowage.fold: z-fold (accordion) along hinge lines parallel to X -> strip 1.626 m wide x 395 m long, 242 layers at the centre; then rolled from both X-tips toward the hub into 2 rolls (axis along Y)
deployment: kick stage (EP, O2) circularises at 0.92 AU, separates
+-X booms extend (articulated-truss canisters or in-situ beam builders), carrying the rolls outward; rolls pay out under brake
+-Y booms extend; their tips pull the outermost accordion panels out to the Y corners; panels unfold
constant-force tensioners take up slack to N = 0.1 N/m; corner vanes unfurl (TRAC booms); terminals unstow (masts)
sun-pointing by vanes; chiplets self-test; film mesh boots region by region
stowage.note: laminate may be ROLLED (strain <= 0.1 % at r >= 34 mm) but never creased: all folds are in the 25 mm glass-cloth hinge strips

segmentation.seams: none: one continuous film (the mesh is unbroken); edges hemmed

electrical.conversion: on-die 2:1 switched-capacitor converter + MPPT -> ~0.5 V core, eta 0.93 (research3 mid)
electrical.service_strings: 1 m2 patches wired 48 half-cells in series (~24 V, Voc ~28 V) for terminals and vane gimbals; below the 80 V sustained-arc threshold (JAXA / NASA Glenn)
electrical.contacts: interdigitated back contacts (IBC): no metal on the front face
electrical.isolation: 50 um laser scribes between half-cells and tiles, glass-filled

chiplet_layout.mesh: 4-neighbour 2D mesh in the rear metal layer, crossing hinge strips on flexible jumpers
chiplet_layout.replica: one 1e8-chip replica per sail, or ~60 frontier-inference patches of 32.5 m, or ~950 small-model patches of 8 m
chiplet_layout.why_back: front placement would shade cells; the Mg spreader and emitter are on the back; front Si+glass (~12 mg/cm2) shields the die from the sunward side

hardware.name: sun_sensor
hardware.note: on boom-tip fittings, looking +Z past the film edge

hardware.name: edge_cable_and_tape

hardware.name: hinge_strips

sail.pointing: 3-axis, non-spinning; 4 corner vanes (2-axis gimbals) give 0.35 N m per axis vs 0.12 N m from a 1 % reflectance asymmetry; star trackers + IMU on the hub, sun sensors at the tips; commands over the film mesh. No liquid-crystal RCDs (organic, need H; not Mercury-native); inorganic MEMS micro-shutter strips are an option.

architecture_reference.note: architecture: 5 um back enamel (eps_b 0.90 assumed). optics.py finds 5 um silicate on Mg gives eps_b ~0.61 (fused-silica floor), so the baseline carries 15 um microtextured enamel (+0.027 kg/m2). If a 5 um enamel reaches eps 0.9, subtract 27 g/m2.

1e26W.note: 1e26 W of CHIP power is unreachable: all film at f=1 gives at most eta_PV*eta_conv*L_sun = 5.14e+25 W. Read as 1e26 W of intercepted sunlight: f = 0.261.

ir.model: incoherent multilayer, Fresnel s/p, hemispherical, Planck-weighted 1.5-60 um at 348 K; fused silica (Franta 25C) used for every glass: pure SiO2 has the deepest reststrahlen gap, so real Mg/Ca/Fe-silicate enamels with broader bands give HIGHER emissivity (this is a conservative floor).

solar_absorptance.note: flat-rear lower bound; textured c-Si cells with metal rear typically absorb 30-70 % of sub-gap light (free carriers + rear metal with light trapping), giving alpha 0.85-0.92. Architecture value 0.90 kept.

rules: Energy per op (J/FLOP) does NOT change sail geometry: area, pitch (at fixed W/site), film, structure and optics are set by sunlight, sheet temperature and PV efficiency. A 10x better J/op gives 10x FLOP/s per sail and, at constant bytes/FLOP of external I/O, 10x link capacity: 10 cm terminals x10 (0.046 kg/m2, +22 % sail mass) or the same count of 30 cm terminals (rate x81 in the far field; ~0.0007 kg/m2).

Memory per site (bytes per W) sets patch and replica AREA: patch side ~ k^-1/2, replica sites ~ k^-1. If the sail is sized to hold the largest replica, its side ~ k^-1/2: k = 10 -> ~88 m, k = 100 -> ~28 m (then the fixed hub/vane mass, ~2.5 % at 279 m, rises to ~25 % and 250 %).
Power per site sets pitch = sqrt(P/q_e): 0.05 W -> 14.7 mm, 0.15 W -> 25.4 mm, 0.5 W -> 46 mm; above ~0.2 W the spreader mass climbs (P^1-2).

energy_basis_check.note: Per-sail FLOP/s uses the architecture basis; the sail geometry does not depend on it (section 2).

power.bus: 800 V DC (glass-insulated Al), 48 V panel strings (< 80 V arc threshold)
power.justification: g/W is flat over 0.3-1 MW (research3 size scan 7.65 -> 7.63); shield mass per W falls as P^-1/3; 4 loops cap a trunk hit at 250 kW; a 1-12 MW training island = 1-12 pods; above ~1 MW bus mass and loop length grow (3 MW: +8 %)

module.description: dense memory + logic stack (technology-agnostic): memory-heavy core with logic, two-phase cold plates, power-delivery planes; outer shell of converters, switches/NICs, loop accumulators and pumps; dedicated Mg-alloy + MgO-SiO2 cast-ceramic shield panels bring every line of sight to the memory to >= 5 g/cm2
module.shield_scaling: dedicated shield mass ~ 50 kg/m2 x 6 (V/P)^(2/3) P^(2/3): per W it falls as P^-1/3, favouring larger pods
module.shield_material: Mg alloy + MgO-SiO2 ceramic (low Z, H-free, Mercury-native). Not sulfur (sublimes ~kg/m2/day at 350 K in vacuum); not Fe as bulk shield (more secondaries per g/cm2, no lower Z/A benefit).

shield.areal: >= 5 g/cm2 on every line of sight to the memory
shield.composition: Mg alloy + MgO-SiO2 ceramic (low Z, H-free, Mercury-native). Not sulfur (sublimes ~kg/m2/day at 350 K in vacuum); not Fe as bulk shield (more secondaries per g/cm2, no lower Z/A benefit).

wings.film: same c-Si film as the sail without chiplets/Mg spreader: glass 20 um / Si 30 um / rear contacts / enamel 15 um, ~0.15 kg/m2 incl. frame
wings.layout: 2 wings in the XY plane (facing +Z), on yoke trusses from x = +-18 m; hinged panels

radiators.layout: YZ plane (faces +-X), knife-edge to the Sun, on +-Y arms, 2 blades in line per arm from y = 20 m, coplanar so they never see each other
radiators.construction: Mg-alloy facesheets 0.15 mm on SO2 heat pipes (Mg tubes 12 mm, 0.10 m pitch, Whipple-bumpered) along Z from a central condenser spine; white Mg/Ca-silicate coating (alpha 0.15-0.2, eps 0.90)

loops.pump: canned-motor centrifugal pump, Fe-Ni, A/B redundant per loop
loops.accumulator: Fe-Ni bellows accumulator, 1 per loop, in the module shield shell
loops.evaporators: two-phase cold plates (Si microchannel) on the memory+logic stack; Tj 105-120 C; stack drop ~25 K
loops.condensers: header ("spine") along each blade at z = 0 with SO2 heat pipes every 0.10 m running +-3 m in Z (fishbone)
loops.isolation: each loop isolatable; a trunk hit loses 25 %, a heat-pipe hit 0.3 m2

DWDM_pod_pod.rate: ~9.6 Tbps each at <= 400 km (Suncatcher-class), near-field at 0.5-2 km

lasers.placement: on a 4 m terminal mast below the module (anti-sun side, z = -4 to -6 m): clear horizon in the wing plane under the wings and blades

propulsion.type: 4 electrodeless RF/ECR ion thrusters on O2 (Mercury-native; no Xe, no H; non-condensable plume)
propulsion.alternatives: SO2 (shares coolant logistics; S deposition risk); Mg/Na metal Hall thrusters rejected: condensable plume coats radiators and PV
propulsion.placement: on 2 short canted booms below the module, plumes 20 deg off the wing plane, away from blades and wings
propulsion.needed: yes: beta dispersion between pods (~5 %) gives ~10.6 m/s/yr of differential drift

mass_breakdown.note: per W of module power; best-credible pod (research3 skeptic checks.py)

dims.projected_footprint_note: cross: wings along X, blades along Y

pod.placement: training/HBM-class islands at 0.86-0.90 AU; service pods (CPU/DRAM sandboxes, storage, gateways) in pod lanes inside the film shell (0.92 AU, +150-300 km outward, >= 2 km lateral of any sail): Starlink-class links need <= ~3,000 km

formation.frame: Hill frame at the cluster reference orbit: x radial (sun line, +x anti-sunward), y along-track, z cross-track
formation.law: projected circular orbit: x = rho/2 cos(nt+phi), y = -rho sin(nt+phi), z = (sqrt3/2) rho cos(nt+phi); constant range rho; projected (y,z) separation never below 0.866*rho*2 sin(pi/N)

baseline.intra_island_link: DWDM 10 cm terminals, 0.5-2 km, near-field (>= 9.6 Tbps each), 6 neighbours per pod

rules: all pods sun-pointing, wings in the plane normal to the Sun; no pod within its neighbours' sun-line cylinder (radius 2 x footprint + 50 m) inside 30 km
islands >= 61 km apart along-track (> 3x pod umbra length of 20 km)
training pods at 0.88 AU are always sunward of the film (0.919+ AU); at >= 6e6 km their penumbra on a sail is < 1e-9 of the disc

handover.rate_model: 10 cm: min(9.6 Tbps, 1.6 Tbps*(1000 km/L)^2); x(D/0.1)^4 in the far field (research3 interconnect fso.py)
handover.finding: Starlink-class sail-pod links close only within ~2000-4000 km. Pods at 0.86-0.90 AU are >= 3e6 km (0.02 AU) from the film: ~1e-4 Gbps on 10 cm. So pods that serve sails (CPU/DRAM sandboxes, storage, gateways) must fly IN the film shell, in pod lanes; HBM training islands may sit at 0.86-0.90 AU and talk to the film only by relay chains.

pod_lane.radial_offset_km: +150 to +300 (anti-sunward of the local sail layer: links look >= 3 deg into the sails' back hemisphere)
pod_lane.lateral_offset_km: >= 2 (outside every sail's penumbra cone: 0.0101 rad x 200 km / 2 + sail/2 + pod/2 ~ 1.2 km)
pod_lane.lane_spacing_km: pods every <= 5643 km along a lane keep >= 1 pod in range of every sail
pod_lane.mass_cost: pods at 0.92 AU instead of 0.88 AU: wing +9 %% area (S 1611 vs 1767 W/m2); research3 r-scan g/W 7.19 (0.90) vs 7.25 (1.00): < 1 %% of pod mass

handover.alternative: matching-beta vane on a pod: extra reflective area ~2.6x the wing (~1.3 % of pod mass at 5 g/m2) makes it co-orbit a sail; rejected for the baseline (huge glinting mirror, shades neighbours), kept as an option for dedicated sail gateways

sun.blender: Sun lamp strength = irradiance (W/m2), angle = angular diameter, colour = Blackbody 5772 K (render/lib.py add_sun)

sail_brightness.note: Front face is near-black navy: ~6.6 stops below an 18% grey card in the same sun. The 4 Al corner vanes are by far the brightest parts (each specular glint ~1x the whole film glint).

glint.geometry: A sun-facing sail reflects the Sun straight back sunward. A viewer sees the glint only near its own ANTISOLAR point: it must be sunward of the sail and look away from the Sun. All sails share (nearly) the same normal, so in a view toward the antisolar point every sail within the glint half-angle of it glints at once: a "glint halo" around the camera's antisolar point.
glint.vane_note: vanes tilt 0-40 deg for control, so their glints point anywhere within ~80 deg of the Sun direction; each vane glints for a random viewer with p ~ 1.3e-04

back_face.note: The back looks anti-sunward, at the sunlit FRONTS of sails farther out (they face the Sun, hence the viewer). Their summed glow (sky coverage g ~ f/2) outshines starlight by ~1e3-1e5x. The back emits ~708 W/m2 at 348 K (LWIR) and has no visible thermal glow (348 K blackbody luminance ~1e-20 cd/m2). Model it as a dark (albedo 0.06) surface under a dim, uniform anti-sun dome plus the Sun-side black sky; it is a silhouette against stars when exposed for sunlit parts.

spacing.model: Poisson in a shell from r_min(f) (sheet 348 K) to 1.1 AU; n = -ln(1-f)/(A_sail * dR); nearest neighbour 0.554 n^-1/3. A thin single layer (all sails at r_min) would give sqrt(A/f) instead; real swarms need ~1e7+ distinct orbit radii to avoid crossings, so the thick-shell numbers are the ones to use for wide shots.

pod_radiators_visible.note: Blades are edge-on: no direct sunlight on the faces. They see the wings only at grazing angles (view factor 0.0026) and the swarm glow. In a frame exposed for sunlit parts the faces are black; only the 25 mm sunward leading edges and the sunward header lips are lit (thin bright white lines). Wings look as dark as sail fronts; the module and booms are the bright, sunlit parts.

lwir.tile_pattern: die hot spots +7-10 K at 25.4 mm pitch, ~1 cm wide

shadows.rule: nothing within 100x its size downstream of any sail; pods sunward of a sail must be >= 300 km away (<0.5 % dimming) or laterally clear of its sun-line cylinder

energy_basis_check.note: Per-sail FLOP/s uses the architecture basis; the sail geometry does not depend on it (section 2).

render_spec.units: metres, kelvin, W/m2; Cycles sun strength = irradiance
render_spec.frame_sail: +Z toward the Sun (light travels -Z); film in XY at z=0; booms along X and Y behind the film
render_spec.frame_pod: +Z toward the Sun; wings in XY along X; radiator blades in the YZ plane along Y
render_spec.exposure: meter an 18 % grey card at 1612 W/m2 (render/lib.py meter); the sail front then sits ~6.6 stops below mid-grey
render_spec.world: black + star field (HYG/BSC); optional anti-sun dome of 4.76e-03 W/m2/sr x (f/0.01) for the swarm glow
render_spec.neighbours: Poisson in a shell r_min(f)..1.1 AU; nearest neighbour 317 km (f=0.01), 139 km (f=0.1), 44 km (f=0.5); all sails share the sun-facing attitude
render_spec.lod: chiplets and scribes only < 5 m; hinge strips as texture stripes beyond ~50 m; booms as lines beyond ~5 km

open_questions: IR emissivity is the largest physics risk. With fused-silica optical constants (a floor), 20 um cover glass gives eps_f ~0.76 and 5 um enamel on Mg gives eps_b ~0.61, against 0.85/0.90 assumed; at 0.76/0.61 the film must sit at 1.04 AU with q_e -22 %. Baseline carries 15 um microtextured Fe/Mg/Ca-silicate enamel (+27 g/m2). Needs measured hemispherical eps of Mercury-composition enamels (5-20 um, textured) at 348 K.

Residual laminate moment (intrinsic film stress of evaporated Mg and deposited glass) must stay <= ~3 K-equivalent, or the hinge-strip edges tilt > 4 deg; fallback stack C (Si spreader) costs +0.02 kg/m2.

Boom deployment: 199 m triangular trusses from a 3.4 m hub have no heritage (largest deployed truss mast ~60 m, SRTM). Options: articulated truss canister or in-situ beam builder from Mg strip; judgement call.

Sail-pod link geometry conflicts with the architecture text: pods at 0.86-0.90 AU are >= 3e6 km from the film, where 10 cm links give ~1e-4 Gbps. Service pods must share the film shell (pod lanes); confirm the split between in-shell service pods and inner training islands.
Laser terminal mass assumed 5 kg (Mercury-built 10 cm); SCOT80 is 11.9 kg per channel. At 12 kg the terminals are 0.011 kg/m2 (+5 % sail mass).
Front-face diffuse albedo: ideal ray optics gives ~0.0006 (cells) but real texture/edge scatter is likely 3-10x higher; render value uses 3x. Needs a measured BRDF of AR-glass/textured c-Si.
Flexible mesh and power jumpers across ~240 hinge lines per sail: fatigue during fold/roll at 100 g launch and deployment.
Thick-shell spacing assumes Poisson placement; a real orbit plan (distinct radii per ring to avoid crossings) changes the neighbour pattern (rings, not random).

Pod shielding depends on stack density: 0.18 g/W at 1.5 m3/MW but 0.8 g/W at 4 m3/MW; with HBM-class parts obsolete by 2070-2300, revisit the 5 g/cm2 requirement against future memory radiation tolerance.
SO2 compatibility with Mg-alloy loop hardware (sulfidation) and O2 ion-thruster lifetime are untested on Mercury-native materials.
1e26 W read as intercepted sunlight (f = 0.26, 1.0e18 sails); 1e26 W of chip power exceeds eta*L_sun = 5.1e25 W and is unreachable.
Porous-silica AR and TiO2 ARC durability under 0.92 AU proton/UV fluence; without AR the glint F0 rises to 3.7 % and q_e drops ~3 %.
